title: A service-provider platform session reads every other provider's capacity profile, quality score and performance-incident log
actor: role_code=service_provider, permissions [bookings.view, scheduling.view, communications.call, communications.message, self_service.view], developmentPreview=false. Authenticated the way the product does: identity_bindings row (identity_source=partner_otp, principal_type=identity_subject, principal_key=provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B, verification_state=verified) + platform_identity_sessions row issued by lib/platform-session.ts issuePlatformSession(), presented as the pawspace_identity_session cookie. PRV-ATTACKER-B has NO row in provider_capacity_profiles at all.
request: Two real layers, both executed. (1) lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest(new Request('https://uat.pawspace.in/api/provider-capacity-control?cityId=blr',{headers:{cookie:pawspace_identity_session=<token>}}), {DB}). (2) app/api/provider-capacity-control/route.ts GET with the same request.
response: (1) GATEWAY ALLOW: {"actor":{"email":"provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B","roleCode":"service_provider","permissions":["bookings.view","scheduling.view","communications.call","communications.message","self_service.view"],"preview":false},"permission":"scheduling.view"} — service_provider holds scheduling.view, so the gateway is satisfied. (2) HANDLER 200 with data.profiles = 20 rows, every provider capacity profile in city blr, e.g. 'groom_arun/Arun R./rating=4.9/quality=96/live=1', 'train_kiran/Kiran S./rating=4.9/quality=95/live=1', 'PRV-VICTIM-A/Victim Grooming Co/rating=4.7/quality=88/live=1'; and data.performance = [{"id":"PERF-1","provider_id":"PRV-VICTIM-A","event_type":"quality_complaint","detail_json":"{\"note\":\"Customer CUST-VICTIM-A complained about handling\",\"severity\":\"high\"}"}]. data.recovery (provider_recovery_cases, LIMIT 50), data.audit (provider_capacity_audit incl. the free-text change `reason`, LIMIT 50) and data.availability (scheduling_availability, LIMIT 200) are returned unfiltered by the same call.
d1_before: provider_capacity_profiles: 20 rows for city_id='blr' (19 seeded by seedProviderCapacityDefaults + PRV-VICTIM-A inserted as the victim, rating=4.7 quality_score=88 capacity=3 max_daily_jobs=5 live=1). provider_performance_events: 1 row PERF-1 (provider_id='PRV-VICTIM-A', event_type='quality_complaint'). identity_bindings: 1 verified partner_otp binding for principal_key='provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B'. No provider_capacity_profiles row exists for PRV-ATTACKER-B.
d1_after: Unchanged — this is a read. (seedProviderCapacityDefaults / ensureSchedulingTables run idempotently on the GET; no row values change.)
repeatable: Yes. Ran twice in the same process: 200 with 20 profiles both times.
canonical_failure: GET /api/provider-capacity-control authorizes on the bare permission `scheduling.view` — which every service_provider session holds — and then returns the whole city's provider roster, quality scores, performance incidents, recovery cases and change audit with no requireProviderOwnership and no provider_id filter, so any onboarded provider reads every competitor's commercial standing.
blast_radius: Every provider with a partner_otp session, against every provider in the same city. Discloses competitor rating, quality_score, capacity, max_daily_jobs, acceptance_timeout, live/status and zone coverage; provider_performance_events detail_json, which carries free-text complaint notes and customer identifiers; provider_capacity_audit, which carries the operator email and the reason text for every stand-down; and provider_recovery_cases. The route-authorization sweep cannot see this: it only probes anonymous and the least-privileged ROLE, and a provider reading another provider's row is a valid role holding the required permission.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-cross-tenant-reads.test.mjs :: "W2-XT (provider-capacity-control): a provider session cannot read the city roster" + "W2-XT (provider-capacity-control): the staff console still works"
fix_note: The capacity CONTROL console's read is raised to scheduling.manage - the permission its own PATCH already required - at BOTH gates: the gateway mapping and the route handler. Nothing in app/** calls this GET, so no provider-facing consumer is lost. scheduling.manage is held by founder, superuser, admin and manager; service_provider does not hold it.
control_gap: The existing route-authorization sweep structurally cannot see this class: it probes anonymous and the LEAST-privileged role, and a provider reading another party's row is a valid role holding the required permission, so the sweep never presents a provider identity at all. The new file issues a real partner_otp platform session.

title: GET /api/food-fulfilment enforces customer ownership on ?customerId but not on ?orderId, so the same row is served to a caller it just refused
actor: role_code=service_provider, permissions [bookings.view, scheduling.view, communications.call, communications.message, self_service.view], developmentPreview=false. Real platform session: verified identity_bindings row (partner_otp / identity_subject / principal_key='provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B') + platform_identity_sessions row from issuePlatformSession(), presented as the pawspace_identity_session cookie. This provider has no relationship of any kind to the food order or to CUST-VICTIM-A.
request: Two requests, same session, same handler (app/api/food-fulfilment/route.ts GET), both first put through the real lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest: (a) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/food-fulfilment?customerId=CUST-VICTIM-A  (b) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/food-fulfilment?orderId=FOOD-A-1
response: (a) GATEWAY ALLOW permission=bookings.view role=service_provider; HANDLER 403 {"error":"Customer ownership denied"}. (b) GATEWAY ALLOW permission=bookings.view role=service_provider; HANDLER 200 {"data":[{"id":"FOOD-A-1","idempotency_key":"idem-a-1","customer_id":"CUST-VICTIM-A","city_id":"blr","zone_id":"blr-east","status":"confirmed","commercial_status":"uat_only","inventory_mode":"uat_seed","delivery_status":"fulfilment_review_required","total_amount":1497,"currency":"INR","created_by":"CUST-VICTIM-A",...,"sku":"food-uat-cat-adult-1kg","item_name":"Adult Cat Food 1kg",...}]} — the identical row the same handler had just refused, plus its lines, reservation, fulfilment, payment and up to 50 fulfilment events.
d1_before: food_orders: 1 row id='FOOD-A-1', customer_id='CUST-VICTIM-A', city_id='blr', zone_id='blr-east', status='confirmed', total_amount=1497. food_order_lines: 1 row FL-1 (3 x food-uat-cat-adult-1kg @499 = 1497). food_inventory_reservations: 1 row FR-1 status='reserved'. identity_bindings: one verified partner_otp binding for 'provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B'; no binding of any kind linking that principal to CUST-VICTIM-A.
repeatable: Yes — deterministic; both calls re-run in the same process give the same 403 / 200 pair.
canonical_failure: food-fulfilment's staff branch runs requireCustomerOwnership only when the caller supplies customerId, so supplying orderId instead reaches listFoodOrders with no ownership predicate and returns another customer's order to any bookings.view holder — the guard is attached to the request parameter rather than to the record that comes back.
blast_radius: Every service_provider platform session (bookings.view is a default service_provider permission and the gateway maps GET /api/food-fulfilment to it), against every food order in the platform, by order id. Discloses customer_id, address zone, order contents, amounts, payment status and the fulfilment event trail. Sibling routes walking-lifecycle / taxi-lifecycle / sitting-lifecycle DO close this by resolving the booking and calling requireProviderOwnership-then-requireCustomerOwnership on the record; food-fulfilment is the one that does not.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-cross-tenant-reads.test.mjs :: "W2-XT (food-fulfilment): ?orderId is guarded exactly as ?customerId is" + "W2-XT (food-fulfilment): staff still read any order, and a customer still reads their own"
fix_note: Ownership is now checked on every record actually RETURNED rather than on the request parameter, which is the convention the sibling walking / taxi / sitting lifecycle routes already follow. A holder of bookings.manage is unaffected; a caller without it sees only their own orders, by whichever parameter they ask.
control_gap: The existing route-authorization sweep structurally cannot see this class: it probes anonymous and the LEAST-privileged role, and a provider reading another party's row is a valid role holding the required permission, so the sweep never presents a provider identity at all. The new file issues a real partner_otp platform session.

title: Any provider session reads every customer's funeral/memorial case, including pickup address and alternate contact, via the unscoped bookings.view branch
actor: role_code=service_provider, permissions [bookings.view, scheduling.view, communications.call, communications.message, self_service.view], developmentPreview=false. Authenticated with a real verified partner_otp identity binding + platform_identity_sessions cookie for principal 'provider:PRV-ATTACKER-B'.
request: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/funeral-memorial  (no scope, no caseId) and GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/funeral-memorial?caseId=FUN-A-1 — each first through the real lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest, then through app/api/funeral-memorial/route.ts GET.
response: Both: GATEWAY ALLOW permission=bookings.view role=service_provider. HANDLER 200. List call body: {"data":[{"id":"FUN-A-1","customer_id":"CUST-VICTIM-A","pet_name":"Bruno","pet_species":"dog","pickup_address":"12 Victim Lane, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038","alternate_contact":"+919800000001","service_type":"cremation_private","memorial_option":"urn","urgency":"urgent","status":"urgent_request",...}], plus funeralSensitiveTemplates. caseId call returns the same record as a single object.
d1_before: funeral_cases: 1 row FUN-A-1 owned by CUST-VICTIM-A with pickup_address='12 Victim Lane, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038' and alternate_contact='+919800000001'. The acting provider has no assignment to that case (assigned_agent_id and vendor_id are both NULL).
canonical_failure: funeral-memorial's non-customer read branch authorizes on the bare permission bookings.view and then lists or fetches any case with no assignment or ownership predicate, and bookings.view is a default service_provider permission — so the branch written as 'staff can see all cases' also admits every provider on the platform.
blast_radius: Every provider session, against every bereavement case on the platform: home pickup address, alternate contact phone, pet name/species, service type and case status. This is the most sensitive customer record surface in the product and it is readable by a party with no relationship to the case. Same defect shape as W2-17-F04 (relocation). The route-authorization sweep cannot see it: bookings.view is not the least-privileged role's permission set, so the sweep never presents a provider identity.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-cross-tenant-reads.test.mjs :: "W2-XT (funeral-memorial): a provider session cannot read another customer's case" + "W2-XT (funeral-memorial): staff can still read the case"
fix_note: The non-customer read branches are gated on customers.view instead of bookings.view. Both are existing platform permissions; the difference is that service_provider holds bookings.view and does not hold customers.view, while founder, superuser, admin, manager and associate do. No new rule - the branch now names the capability the platform already defines for reading customer records.
control_gap: The existing route-authorization sweep structurally cannot see this class: it probes anonymous and the LEAST-privileged role, and a provider reading another party's row is a valid role holding the required permission, so the sweep never presents a provider identity at all. The new file issues a real partner_otp platform session.
